title: Result Types and Explicit Failure Handling knowledge check

questions.prompt: What should a reliable TypeScript integration do with external data?
options: Treat JSON.parse as a validation step.
Validate data and failures at runtime, while using types to make trusted application contracts explicit.
Assume the declared type validates the server response.
Ignore promise rejections and malformed data.
questions.answer_key: Validate data and failures at runtime, while using types to make trusted application contracts explicit.
questions.explanation: Types and runtime validation solve different problems at external boundaries.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Result Types and Explicit Failure Handling”?
options: The concept should be demonstrated with success and failure unions and checked against its intended contract.
The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with success and failure unions and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Success and failure unions”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Result Types and Explicit Failure Handling”?
options: Assume exhaustively handling results is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
Check modeling errors as return values, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.answer_key: Check modeling errors as return values, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Modeling errors as return values”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
